LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How should you read for comprehension?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. answer comprehension questions from a text for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Answer comprehension questions from a text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to answer comprehension questions from a text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer comprehension questions from a text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer comprehension questions from a text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: answer comprehension questions from a text for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: answer comprehension questions from a text for information.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How should you read for comprehension?
2. Why are community heroes and heroines important in the society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: answer comprehension questions from a text for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
